bib.title: ACM: Agentic Context Management for Long Horizon Tasks

legacy_report:
COVERAGE: All 24 pages read (86,217 chars via pypdf). Prompts in Appendix B were skimmed, not read line by line. The extraction was clean. No embedded instructions found.

SOURCE: "ACM: Agentic Context Management for Long Horizon Tasks". Xiaochuan Li*, Ryan Ming*, Meng Chu, Shuai Shao, Rong Jin, Chenyan Xiong. Carnegie Mellon University (Li, Ming, Chu, Xiong) and Meta (Shao, Jin). Preprint, arXiv 2607.23809v1, cs.AI, 26 Jul 2026. A footnote says all experiments were run at CMU and Meta only advised. No venue is stated.

MAIN CLAIM: The agent should decide when to compress its own context. It gets two tools: `manage_context`, which summarizes everything since the last call and saves the raw messages to disk under a summary id, and `query_memory`, which retrieves from those raw messages by id. This is compared with a "summary agent" that an external monitor forces to compress at a fixed usage threshold (Fig 1 example: 90% of the window). The paper also trains the model on when to call the tools. The abstract says the paper builds a "post-training pipeline".

HEADLINE NUMBERS (Table 2, Pass@1; student, summarizer and querier are all Qwen3.5-9B; teacher is Qwen3.5-397B-A17B):
1. BrowseComp-Plus: ReAct 0.570, ReSum 0.608, ACON 0.614, ACE 0.589, ACM untrained 0.635, ACM post-trained 0.727. The test set is 150 questions, and the training set is 680. Fig 4/5 give n=4x150 runs for Qwen3.5-9B. The paper claims +27% relative over ReAct (0.727/0.570).
2. Peak tokens on BrowseComp-Plus: ReAct 63k, ReSum 68k, ACM post-trained 54k. On the other benchmarks:
   - DeepSearchQA (out-of-domain, live web search): Pass@1 0.367 (ReAct) to 0.425; peak tokens 46K to 41K.
   - SWE-Bench Verified (trained on SWE-Gym): Pass@1 0.489 to 0.530; peak tokens 59k to 50K.
   - The text says "around 20%" lower peak tokens. That does not match every column.
3. Untrained GPT-5.5 under ACM makes near-zero `manage_context` and `query_memory` calls (Fig 4, n=1x150). Post-trained 9B makes the most calls. The paper reads this as models lacking the proactivity to manage context without training.
4. Pass^4 (all four runs correct, a consistency measure) on BrowseComp-Plus, read from Fig 5 labels: ReAct 34.1, ACM post-trained epoch 3 59.3. Pass@4 moves 73.5 to 82.0. The paper says the gain is mostly reliability, not a wider capability boundary.

Table 3 ablation: GPT-5.5 distillation alone gives 0.623 on BrowseComp-Plus, below untrained ACM (0.635). ACM data alone gives 0.727, and both together 0.734.

QUOTES:
- p.7: "ACM agents learn to compress context proactively: the characteristic sawtooth pattern shows that compression is triggered well before the context limit, driven by the agent's own reasoning state."
- p.7: "even strong models may lack the proactivity to manage their own context without dedicated training."

LIMITS (authors' own, p.9, plus my observations):
- Authors: it needs a base model strong enough for long rollouts. Appendix D shows Qwen3-4B-thinking collapses to 2-turn rollouts (3.4% vs 57.3% accuracy for 9B), so compression never comes into play.
- Authors: the baselines (ReSum, ACON, ACE) were re-implemented by the authors and may differ from the originals.
- My observation: the Summary Agent threshold is described only as an example (90%). I did not find the actual threshold used in the experiments.
- My observation: no confidence intervals, no cost or latency figures, and no prefix-cache analysis, although `manage_context` rewrites history.
- My observation: only one student model size was used (9B), so scale is not tested. The teacher is much larger.
- My observation: the sawtooth plot (Fig 3) is single-benchmark. Fig 6 is a single case study.
- The paper does not compare agent-chosen timing against a tuned threshold or phase-boundary trigger trained on the same data. Its summary-agent baselines are also not given the lossless offload, so the gains from trigger timing and from lossless retrieval are not separated.

BUILDS ON: ReAct (Yao et al., 2022); ReSum (Wu et al., 2025); ACON (Kang et al., 2025); ACE (Zhang et al., 2026); Mem1 (Zhou et al., 2025); SUPO (Lu et al., 2025); AgentFold (Ye et al., 2025, closest work, data pipeline not public); MemGPT-style memory (Packer et al., 2023); on-policy distillation (Lu and Lab, 2025); Pass^k (Yao et al., 2024); benchmarks BrowseComp-Plus (Chen et al., 2025), DeepSearchQA (Gupta et al., 2026), SWE-Bench Verified (Jimenez et al., 2024).

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Fig 3 (p.7), input tokens per turn, ACM vs ReAct, with the 128K limit. It shows the agent-chosen sawtooth that stays well under the limit. Fig 1 (p.3) contrasts ReAct, forced-threshold summary and ACM.

RELEVANCE TO NOTE: Supports "Trigger points" (agent-chosen timing beats a fixed threshold in these tests). It also supports "Letting the model edit its own context" (lossless offload plus retrieval). The note's "Compacting only at overflow" and "~80%" guidance is not tested here.
